newsitem.title: POLAND: Universal makes late bid for Ruch.
newsitem.headline: Universal makes late bid for Ruch.

text.p: Polish trader Universal SA has sent a letter to the treasury ministry expressing interest in buying part of Poland's largest news-stand chain, Ruch SA, a ministry spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

Malgorzata Szyszllo told Reuters that no decision had been made on the proposal, which the daily Rzeczpospolita said on Tuesday envisioned reducing the percentage a consortium led by France's Hachette had agreed to buy.

"(Treasury) Minister (Miroslaw) Pietrewicz is getting acquainted with the offer submitted in the letter from Universal, which is all we have to say right now," Szyszllo said, adding that a decision would not come before Thursday.
Last week deputy treasury minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said the Hachette consortium, which includes Elektrim and Echo Investment, would likely buy Ruch in January.
Rzeczpospolita said Hachette would pay $55 million for 51 percent of Ruch, and could later up its stake based on investment pledges.
The paper said the Universal proposal saw Hachette taking 40 percent and a consortium led by Universal 20 percent.

Employees would take 15 percent, the ministry would retain five percent, and 20 percent would be floated on the Warsaw bourse. No officials close to the offer at Universal were immediately available for comment.
Ruch has a 65 percent share of Poland's press distribution market and owns 17,000 news-stands nationwide.
Its net profit in 1995 was 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys. -- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
